name: Kentucky

code.name: Kentucky Revised Statutes (KRS)
code.edition: KRS as the Kentucky General Assembly's site prints it: 'Includes enactments through the 2026 Regular Session', database last updated 11/06/2026 (chapter page); each section prints its own effective date

ky-118.425.citation: KRS 118.425 (issuance of certificates of election; tie votes), effective June 27, 2025

ky-120.157.citation: KRS 120.157 (automatic recount; determination by State Board of Elections; costs), effective June 29, 2021

ky-120.185.citation: KRS 120.185 (recount of election of officers referred to in KRS 120.155; petition), effective June 29, 2021

ky-120.155.citation: KRS 120.155 (contest of regular election of officers other than Governor, Lieutenant Governor, General Assembly member and certain city officers), effective June 29, 2021

ky-120.250.citation: KRS 120.250 (contest or recount of election on public question), effective January 2, 1978

ky-117.305.citation: KRS 117.305 (recanvass of votes; discrepancy or written request)

ties.applies_to: the State Board of Elections issues the certificates of election where the successful candidate was voted for by the state at large, by a district greater than one county, or was a candidate for member of Congress or the General Assembly
ties.steps: the certificate of election goes to the candidate with the highest number of votes; if two or more persons are found to have the highest and an equal number of votes for the same office, the election is determined by lot in the manner the board directs, in the presence of not less than three other persons

sources.quote: If two (2) or more persons are found to have received the highest and an equal number of votes for the same office, the election shall be determined by lot in the manner the board directs, in the presence of not less than three (3) other persons.

The State Board of Elections shall issue certificates of election where the successful candidate was voted for by the state at large, was voted for by a district greater than one (1) county, or was a candidate for member of Congress or the General Assembly.

ties.note: Subsection (6) says 'the board' and 'the same office' without limiting the kind of office; the board in (1) and (5) is the State Board of Elections, so it is read as covering these offices. The General Assembly is also judge of the election of its members (KRS 120.195, 120.215, listed in the chapter contents, not read).

ties.applies_to: electors for President and Vice President
ties.steps: the State Board of Elections issues a certificate of election to each elector of the party whose candidates for President and Vice President received the highest number of votes; for a tie, subsection (6)'s lot is read to apply

sources.quote: In the case of elections for electors of President and Vice President of the United States, the board shall issue a certificate of election to each elector of the political party or organization whose candidates for President and Vice President received the highest number of votes

If two (2) or more persons are found to have received the highest and an equal number of votes for the same office, the election shall be determined by lot in the manner the board directs, in the presence of not less than three (3) other persons.

ties.note: The section does not say what a tie between presidential tickets does; the lot sentence precedes the electors sentence in the same subsection and is read to reach it [inferred].

ties.applies_to: county, city and school-district offices: where the successful candidate was voted for by the electors of one county or of a district less than one county (county board of elections), or of a city or school district extending beyond one county (the county board of the candidate's residence)
ties.steps: if the county board of elections finds that two or more candidates have received the highest and equal number of votes for the same office, it determines by lot which candidate is elected

sources.quote: If the board finds that two (2) or more candidates have received the highest and equal number of votes for the same office, the board shall determine by lot which of the candidates is elected.
the county board of elections shall issue certificates of election where the successful candidate was voted for by the electors of one (1) county, or of a district less than one (1) county

ties.note: State general law only; city and special-district charters and the Kentucky provisions for city officers were not read.

ties.applies_to: a primary tie; a tie on a public question
ties.note: Read: KRS 118.425 (certificates of election; tie votes) in full and the contents list of chapter 118 (where 118.425 is the only section titled for tie votes), and the contents of chapter 120 and sections 120.095, 120.155, 120.157, 120.185, 120.250. 118.425 speaks of certificates of election; whether it governs a primary (the section about nominations by primary was not read) and what a tied public question does were not found. The sentence in 118.425(6) may or may not reach a primary; this is not claimed.

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for the office
threshold.conditions: applies to members of the General Assembly, the U.S. Senate and House, Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Commissioner of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics, Secretary of State and Attorney General; the State Board of Elections determines whether a recount is required from the total votes certified to the Secretary of State; the county boards of elections conduct it
threshold.in_words: a candidate defeated by a margin of not more than one-half of one percent of the votes cast for the office makes a recount mandatory

who_may_request: no request: required by the statute

sources.quote: In any regular election or special election for any member of the General Assembly, the United States Senate or the United States House of Representatives, Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Commissioner of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics, Secretary of State, and Attorney General, a recount of the vote shall be required when a candidate is defeated by a margin of not more than one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the votes cast for the office.
The costs of any recount held pursuant to this section shall be paid by the Commonwealth of Kentucky.
The State Board of Elections shall determine whether a recount is required under this section based upon the total number of votes certified to the Secretary of State.

recounts.note: 'Not more than' is inclusive. The section lists the offices; the presidency, other statewide offices not listed, local offices, primaries and public questions are not covered by it. It dates from 2021 Ky. Acts ch. 197 (effective June 29, 2021).

threshold.conditions: for a candidate who does not qualify for the automatic recount: a slate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, or a candidate for the U.S. Senate or House, petitions the Franklin Circuit Court (governor: not later than the Tuesday following the election; Congress: not later than the second Tuesday); a candidate for the General Assembly petitions the Circuit Court of the county where the candidate resides, not later than the second Tuesday following the election; the requester executes a bond with approved surety for the costs, in an amount fixed by the Circuit Judge
threshold.in_words: a candidate who is not entitled to the automatic recount may petition the court for a recount whatever the margin, on a bond for the costs

who_may_request: a slate of candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor
a candidate for the United States Senate or House
a candidate for the General Assembly
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by bond fixed by the Circuit Judge

sources.quote: Any slate of candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, or any candidate for the United States Senate or the United States House of Representatives who was voted for at a regular election or a special election, and who does not qualify for an automatic recount under KRS 120.157, may request a recount of the ballots by filing a petition in the Franklin Circuit Court.

Any candidate for the General Assembly who was voted for at a regular election or special election, and who does not qualify for an automatic recount under KRS 120.157, may request a recount of the ballots by filing a petition in the Circuit Court of the county where the requesting candidate resides.
The party requesting the recount shall execute bond with approved surety for the costs of the recount, in an amount to be fixed by the Circuit Judge.

recounts.note: No margin condition appears in 120.185 (the only condition is not qualifying for the automatic recount), so a candidate beyond the automatic margin may still petition [as written]. Findings of the court on these offices are advisory to the General Assembly or Congress (120.185(2)(e), (3)(d)), litigation not recorded here.

threshold.conditions: any candidate for a state, county, district or city office (other than Governor, Lieutenant Governor, the General Assembly, and certain city offices) who does not qualify for an automatic recount petitions the court where contest petitions are filed, not later than ten days after the election (certificate from the county board) or the second Tuesday following the election (certificate from the State Board); bond with approved surety fixed by the Circuit Judge
threshold.in_words: a candidate for a state, county, district or city office may petition for a recount whatever the margin, on a bond for the costs

who_may_request: any candidate voted for at a regular election for an office to which KRS 120.155 applies
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by bond fixed by the Circuit Judge

sources.quote: Any candidate who was voted for at a regular election for any of the offices to which KRS 120.155 applies, and who does not qualify for an automatic recount under KRS 120.157, may request a recount of the ballots by filing a petition with the same court where petitions of contest are required to be filed.

Any candidate for election to any state, county, district or city office (except the office of Governor, Lieutenant Governor, member of the General Assembly, and those city offices as to which there are other provisions made by law for determining contest elections)
shall file his or her petition requesting a recount not later than ten (10) days after the day of the election.
The party requesting the recount shall execute bond with approved surety for the costs of the recount, in an amount to be fixed by the Circuit Judge.

recounts.note: State general law only; the 'other provisions made by law' for certain city offices were not read.

threshold.conditions: petition filed with the court where contest petitions are filed, within ten days after the day of the primary; bond with approved surety fixed by the Circuit Judge
threshold.in_words: any candidate voted for at a primary may petition for a recount whatever the margin, on a bond for the costs

who_may_request: any candidate voted for at a primary
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by bond fixed by the Circuit Judge

sources.quote: Any candidate voted for at a primary held under KRS 118.015 to 118.035 and 118.105 to 118.255 may request a recount of the ballots by filing a petition with the same court that contest petitions are required to be filed with, within ten (10) days after the day of the primary
The party requesting the recount shall execute a bond with approved surety for the costs of the recount, in an amount to be fixed by the Circuit Judge.

recounts.note: The automatic recount of 120.157 does not apply to primaries.

threshold.conditions: any elector who was qualified to and did vote on a public question submitted to the voters of a county, city or district (other than a constitutional amendment or a local option question under KRS chapter 242) files a petition with the clerk of the Circuit Court within thirty days after the election; the court requires the contestants to give bond for costs
threshold.in_words: any elector who voted on a local public question may demand a recount of the ballots whatever the margin, within thirty days, on a bond for costs

who_may_request: any elector who was qualified to and did vote on the public question
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioners, by bond for costs (the court requires contestants to give bond for costs)

sources.quote: Any elector who was qualified to and did vote on any public question, other than a constitutional amendment or a question of local option under KRS Chapter 242, submitted to the voters of any county, city or district for their approval or rejection may contest the election or demand a recount of the ballots by filing a petition, within thirty (30) days after the election, with the clerk of the Circuit Court of the county in which the election was held

recounts.note: A local public question only. Statewide questions and constitutional amendments are dealt with in KRS 120.280 to 120.300, a contest procedure that includes a recount of ballots (120.290, read), whose terms were not recorded as a rule.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes which were cast for such office
threshold.conditions: a recanvass (a re-check of the voting equipment and certain ballots of the precincts involved, not a hand recount); a candidate's written request must be made before 4 p.m. on the Tuesday following a primary or regular election (the county clerk or county board of elections may also order one for a discrepancy); the request compels the recanvass only if the candidate's difference from any other candidate is less than 1% of the total votes cast for the office
threshold.in_words: a candidate within less than one percent of the total votes cast for the office may compel a recanvass of the voting equipment by a written request

who_may_request: a candidate who has filed with the county clerk (to the county board of elections) or with the Secretary of State (to the Secretary of State)
the county clerk or county board of elections on noticing a discrepancy in the tally
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the part read

sources.quote: A candidate's written request for a recanvass shall be insufficient to compel the recanvass unless the difference between the number of votes received by the requesting candidate and the number of votes received by any other candidate or candidates for the same office is less than one percent (1%) of the total votes which were cast for such office.
unless before 4 p.m. on the Tuesday following a primary or regular election

or a candidate makes a written request to the county board of elections in the case of a candidate who has filed with the county clerk, or the Secretary of State in the case of a candidate who has filed with the Secretary of State, to check and recanvass the voting equipment

recounts.note: Typed 'other' because a recanvass re-adds the machine and absentee returns and is not a recount of the ballots. For Governor and Lieutenant Governor no recanvass is made when the automatic recount applies (120.157(2)(a), read).

unread.what: KRS 120.195 and 120.215 (contest by a candidate for the General Assembly, and the General Assembly's board), 120.280 to 120.300 (statewide questions and constitutional amendments), the primary nomination sections of chapter 118, and city-officer provisions
unread.reason: not read; contests are litigation (brief), and the other sections were outside the tie and recount sections found directly

notes: Kentucky was read at the General Assembly's statute pages: sections 118.425, 117.305, 120.095, 120.155, 120.157, 120.185, 120.250 and 120.290, and the contents lists of chapters 118 and 120.

The earlier reader's lead (research/historical-close-races-v2.md 3a and 3b) is borne out: lot for a tie (118.425(6)) and an automatic recount at not more than one-half of one percent (120.157, effective June 29, 2021); it also gave 'requested, no margin, with a bond' (120.185), confirmed. New here: the recanvass at under one percent (117.305), and the automatic recount covers only the offices it lists, not primaries or local offices.
